did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with the heading, “For the music director. Of David. A psalm, a song,” identifying it as a psalm intended for the music director and attributed to David.
Did you know? This verse uses the title “He who rides through the clouds,” along with the call to praise God’s name: “His name is Yah.”
Did you know? The psalm describes God as “a father to the fatherless” and “a defender of widows,” emphasizing his care for the vulnerable and defenseless.
Did you know? The description of the Lord going before his people places the wilderness—“the desert”—as the setting for his journey and guidance of Israel.
Did you know? The revelation at Sinai is portrayed as a powerful event in which the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the God of Israel.
Did you know? This verse says that the Lord gives the word of salvation, and that the women who proclaim it are “a great host”—a large group spreading the good news.
Did you know? God’s chariots are described in enormous numbers: “tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands,” and the verse also connects the Lord’s presence with Mount Sinai in the sanctuary.
Did you know? The verse describes ascending on high, taking captives, and receiving gifts from people; it concludes by stating the purpose of God’s dwelling: “that the Lord God may dwell there.”
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes the Lord’s daily help: “day by day” he carries our burdens, and he is the God of our salvation.
Did you know? Near the end of the psalm, the kingdoms of the earth are called to sing to God and praise him, so that worship expands from Israel to all nations.
